# Open statements of the single proof

<!-- Generated by scripts/one_proof/render_open.py from open-statements.json (the Lean build), kinds.tsv,
claims.tsv, reviews.tsv, credits.tsv and issues.json. Do not edit by hand: edit those, or regenerate the JSON
after a fold. -->

`ZInQ.OneProof.frozenTarget` (`ZInQKernel/OneProof/Main.lean`) is a Lean theorem, checked by the kernel with no
`sorry` and only the standard axioms, that proves the frozen target `ZInQ.FrozenTarget`, the theorem that Z is
Diophantine in Q (the 11/5 manuscript, Theorem 1.1), from the hypotheses below. Everything else is proved.
It is the headline `ZInQ.exists_bounded_integer_polynomial_defining_integers_of_sixContactMin_poleCompleteness`
(`SixContactMin` and the manuscript's Theorem 5.2, `PoleCompleteness`, the argument `hPC`) applied to the H bundles.
Each hypothesis is a Lean `Prop`; proving one in Lean, or reducing it to statements printed in the literature,
removes it. See
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how to contribute and check a proof.

**19 hypotheses of the H part** (in the bundles `OpenAddedLeaves30`, `OpenResearchLeaves78`), plus three hypotheses outside the H part (`hRC`, `hCT`, `hRank`, from which Lean proves pole completeness, Theorem 5.2 of the 11/5 manuscript), listed at the end.

* **Strict count: 8 published / 11 glue** (the strictest flagged reading; no hypothesis carries a strictest-reading flag).
* LEAF means a published, refereed theorem stated over genuine definitions in its printed form, or a direct
  instance of it (a special case that needs no argument). GLUE is everything else: a consequence of one theorem,
  a composite of several, project glue, or a leaf whose published form is still pending a reading (`kinds.tsv`,
  column `flag`).
* By kind: consequence 10, published 9.

## Kernel-wide readings

Readings that apply to every statement built on a shared kernel definition.

* **Published means read.** A hypothesis counts as published only after a reader has checked it against the printed
  page; unread and unverified rows count as glue (ruling 2026-11-17). With no human reader available, an
  adversarial AI reading in three independent lenses stands in for the human one (ruling 2026-11-26,
  STATEMENT-CHECKS.md, "Adversarial AI readings").
* **B_dR.** The manuscript uses `B_dR` in its invariant spaces (L10984–L10992) without defining the ring. Use
  Brinon–Conrad (provenance (b), the manuscript's `brinon-conrad`), Def. 4.4.7, p. 60 and the discussion on p. 131,
  before Def. 9.1.4 (which defines B_cris), for `B_dR` and the `B_dR^+[1/t]` presentation. The kernel's ring is
  Mathlib's `BDeRham 𝓞_ℂ_[p] p`: the `ZInQ.Contrib.G9.PkgI4.BdR`, `ZInQ.Contrib.G9.BdrKer.BdR`, `HDec.PkgI4.BdR`,
  and `ZInQKernel/OneProof/H/TailC.lean` copies are each definitionally equal to it. The positive ring is Mathlib's
  `BDeRhamPlus`, the completion of `W(PreTilt 𝓞_ℂ_[p])[1/p]` at `ker θ`. In `ZInQ.Contrib.G9.BdrKer.Cp`,
  `ker_fontaineTheta_Cp` and `ker_fontaineThetaInvertP_Cp` supply the generator `xi = p - [p-flat]` before and after
  inverting `p`; `isAdicComplete_BDeRhamPlus`, `isDiscreteValuationRing_BDeRhamPlus`, and `maximalIdeal_BDeRhamPlus`
  give the complete DVR and its maximal ideal. `isFractionRing_BDeRham` and `bdREquivAway` match the fraction field
  and the presentation inverting `xi`. The period `t = log[ε]` is `DeRhamPrint.TDict.tt`;
  `DeRhamPrint.BdRT.tt_eq_logTeich` identifies it with `HDec.PkgI4.BergerBst.logTeich` for the same `ε`, and
  `DeRhamPrint.BdRT.fontaineT_reading` gives `t ≠ 0`, the uniformizer properties, and `σ(t) = χ(σ)t`. The `[1/t]`
  presentation is matched by `DeRhamPrint.TDict.bdREquivAwayT`. Its Galois action is `DeRhamPrint.BdRT.awayTAction`,
  extending the action on the positive ring by `DeRhamPrint.BdRT.awayTAct_comp` and matching the kernel's `bdrAct`
  by `DeRhamPrint.BdRT.bdREquivAwayT_intertwines`. A print defining B_dR as B_dR^+[1/t] is now matched by proved
  lemmas (TDict.bdREquivAwayT, BdRT.fontaineT_reading), so reading a statement through that definition no longer
  makes it GLUE. The row whose statement reaches `B_dR` is `scholzeH1AbVar` (`DeRhamScholze.HTMerge.ScholzeH1AbVar`,
  over `DeRhamScholze.ddrFam`, `D_dR = (B_dR ⊗ W)^{G_F}`, and `DeRhamScholze.filD`, `Fil^j D_dR = D_dR ∩ (t^j B_dR^+
  ⊗ W)`); its rating is unchanged. `deRhamVpAbVarDirect` is no longer a row: it is derived from `scholzeH1AbVar` and
  `t10TateDuality` (`DeRhamScholze.HTMerge.deRhamVpAbVarDirect_of_scholzeH1Milne`, fork PR #106). Fontaine,
  *Astérisque* 223, Exp. II is outside the manuscript's bibliography and unread. Berger 2002 §1.2 is UNVERIFIED as a
  locator for this definition.

## How to help

* **Prove a statement in Lean**: pick a row whose status is open or "project interest, free to claim", claim
  it on [issue #14](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/14) with a line `Claiming <field> at <commit>`
  (the field name as in the first column), and follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).
* **Check a statement against its printed source** (no Lean needed): pick a packet below and follow
  [STATEMENT-CHECKS.md](STATEMENT-CHECKS.md). [pages-wanted.md](pages-wanted.md) lists the printed pages a
  reader can check.
* Tiers come from a model triage that no person has reviewed yet; treat them as a rough guide.
* The project logs its folds and landings on [issue #3](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/3).

## Packets

A packet is a set of statements decided by reading one block of the literature. Claim a packet with a line
`Claiming reading <packet>` on its own issue if it has one, otherwise on the statement-checks issue, and until that issue is opened on [issue #14](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/14); see [STATEMENT-CHECKS.md](STATEMENT-CHECKS.md).

### Packet R1

Reduction block: SGA 7 I Exp. IX, BLR 1.2 Prop. 4, Serre-Tate 1968. Claim it on [Deicyde #14](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/14).

> r16-det: Diamond-Shurman Thm 9.6.5 at k = 2 for the Section 9.5 realization on A_f, over K_{f,lambda}, universal over A_f. For every (A, pi, theta) that is DS's A_f (afShimura's characterization, for any X, generators, P0, Jacobian and Hecke operators as in heckeJ1DS), every prime l and every place lambda | l of K_f: for p not dividing N l every arithmetic Frobenius sigma at p acting on V_lambda = K_lambda (x)_{Q_l (x) K_f} V_l(A) (rho_{f,lambda}, DS Exercise 9.5.2(a)) has characteristic polynomial X^2 - a_p X + chi(p) p over K_lambda. Statement = aftate-fix2's AfTateLam.AfTateDSLambda verbatim (AfTateLam.afCharpolyDS965_iff, Iff.rfl); it implies r16-close's glue AfDetLambda (AfTateLam.afDetLambda_of_ds965).

## Hypotheses outside the H part

These are `frozenTarget`'s other arguments (outside the H bundles); they are not part of the counts above.
Pole completeness PC (`ZInQ.PoleCompleteness`) is Theorem 5.2 of the 11/5 manuscript for its own pole
polynomial. Lean proves it from these by the manuscript's descent (Section 5.1):
`ZInQ.Manuscript.PoleS12.poleCompleteness_of_restrictedConverseGenuine_casselsTatePairing`
(`ZInQKernel/Contrib/OneProof/CasselsTatePairing.lean`). Only `hRC`, the restricted converse (Theorem 5.3), is
the manuscript's own theorem; each entry's kind says what the others are. The former Route K inputs
(Tian–Yuan–Zhang and Gross–Zagier) are no longer hypotheses.
